articles.headline: Tyrese Haliburton: No restrictions in return from Achilles tear
articles.description: Pacers star guard Tyrese Haliburton says he won't have any restrictions as he returns from the torn Achilles that has kept him off the court for more than a year.
articles.body:
Indiana Pacers star guard Tyrese Haliburton said he won't have any restrictions as he returns from the torn Achilles that has kept him off the court for more than a year.

"I am healthy. I am 100%. There will be no restrictions," Haliburton told reporters at Pacers media day Monday. "That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I'm good. I'm ready to go for the year."

Haliburton suffered the right Achilles tear in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals after he tried to play through a calf strain during the Pacers' best shot at a first title. He sat out the 2025-26 season while recovering as the team languished through a franchise-worst 19-63 campaign.

Pacers coach Rick Carlisle was a bit more conservative about the plan for Haliburton, saying decisions would be made in consultation with the training staff. Carlisle, however, indicated he did not expect Haliburton to be held back much, if at all.

"At this point, it really appears that he has made a great recovery and a great return to play," Carlisle told reporters.

"Do not anticipate a lot of limitations, but we will make sure that we go at the correct pace."

With Haliburton back at full strength to rejoin a team whose major move last season was a deadline trade for center Ivica Zubac, the Pacers are looking to be a contender once again.

"I've worked really hard to get to where I am right now," Haliburton said. "I'm a big believer in my work.

"I've put in an unbelievable amount of time to get to where I am today, so all my belief comes from that."

articles.headline: Cowboys' Jalen Thompson to be sidelined with hamstring injury
articles.description: Cowboys safety Jalen Thompson could be sidelined four-plus weeks because of a hamstring injury he suffered in Sunday's loss to the Ravens, executive vice president Stephen Jones said Monday.
articles.body:
RIO DE JANEIRO -- For the third straight game the Dallas Cowboys have a lost a safety for multiple games due to injury.

Jalen Thompson was knocked from the 34-31 loss against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday with a hamstring injury with 7:40 left in the first half when he was caught in an awkward spot on a Derrick Henry run.

Speaking on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Monday, executive vice president Stephen Jones said Thompson could miss "four-plus weeks." He is scheduled for an MRI after the team's return to Dallas earlier Monday morning.

"We've been hit there [at safety], no question," Jones said, adding, "We're needing every last one of them right now because of the injuries."

In the season opener against the New York Giants, Malik Hooker suffered a broken forearm and is recovering from surgery. He could return as soon as next week against the Houston Texans. Last week, P.J. Locke suffered a torn plantar fascia and he was placed on injured reserve on Saturday. The earliest he can return is Oct. 26 against the Philadelphia Eagles.

In March, Thompson signed the richest free agent deal the Cowboys have given out in more than a decade at three years, $33 million. He started the first two games and entered Sunday's game as the defense's second-leading tackler.

It is possible Hooker could return this week against the Houston Texans, but if he does not, then the Cowboys are down to Caleb Downs, Markquese Bell and Alijah Clark at safety. Bell missed time against the Ravens because of dehydration.

Jones said the Cowboys will look to see if there is a way to "shore up" the position with Locke and Thompson out for a prolonged time.

articles.headline: McCarthy exits Vikings as one of franchise's biggest draft busts
articles.description: J.J. McCarthy was the No. 10 pick in 2024 but played only 10 games before being traded to the Giants on Monday.
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Less than two years ago, Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell appeared on the "Rich Eisen Show" and uttered 12 words that will be dissected in Minnesota for years to come.

"I believe that organizations fail young quarterbacks before young quarterbacks fail organizations," O'Connell said during the interview, which took place in September 2024. 

Two years later, it's fair to ask: Does that explain Monday's news that the Vikings traded J.J. McCarthy for a fifth-round pick after only two seasons, 10 games and 243 pass attempts? Is that why McCarthy is now headed to the New York Giants to resurrect his career at an age -- 23 years, 9 months -- that makes him younger than most of the quarterbacks drafted this spring? Did the Vikings organization fail him?

Or was McCarthy simply a spectacularly historic draft bust who wouldn't have made it no matter which organization drafted him?

The truth is that no key player in this debacle -- arguably the biggest personnel miss in franchise history -- is without blame. 

The general manager who drafted McCarthy, Kwesi Adofo-Mensah, was fired in January. He and O'Connell put McCarthy on the field before he was ready. And before anyone saw anything close to a finished version of the player, the team's remaining decision-makers -- O'Connell, former interim general manager Rob Brzezinski and new general manager Nolan Teasley -- rendered a final judgment on him. 

Even owners Zygi and Mark Wilf absorb some of the responsibility. Their insistence on never taking a competitive step back usually provides fans with entertaining seasons, but it is not conducive to giving young quarterbacks sufficient time to develop. Sam Darnold took over when McCarthy missed his rookie season with a knee injury. McCarthy undeniably played better at the end of his 10-game stint last season than at the beginning, and in a more forgiving environment, O'Connell and Teasley might have had more patience. 

In a conversation this summer, former Vikings coach Brad Childress recalled a standard articulated by Hall of Fame coach Bill Walsh and still makes sense today: Give a promising young quarterback 24 games -- one full season and a half of a second, in the days of a 16-game schedule -- before deciding the next steps. During the offseason, the Vikings added free agent Kyler Murray, who is now starting, pushing McCarthy to QB3 behind No. 2 Carson Wentz.

McCarthy, for his part, made some clear mistakes beyond his obvious poor performance. His frenetic play style contributed to four injuries that limited his development, and it contributed to his status as the only quarterback in the NFL's modern draft era to be selected in the first round and miss his entire rookie season for health reasons. During his time in Minnesota, McCarthy suffered knee and ankle injuries, as well as a concussion, while running outside of the pocket. articles.headline: Karl-Anthony Towns wants extension to stay with Knicks
articles.description: Karl-Anthony Towns said he wants to get a contract extension done with the Knicks as he has one year and a player option left on his contract.
articles.body:
TARRYTOWN, N.Y. -- Karl-Anthony Towns reiterated his desire to get a contract extension done while acknowledging the potential discomfort this season could bring as the New York Knicks look to defend their NBA title.

"I've made it known I want to play here," Towns said Monday at media day. "I've been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done and step on the floor and feel as comfortable as possible."

Towns is eligible for a four-year deal worth over $276 million, but it doesn't appear something will get done before the season starts. He is due $57 million this season and has a $61.1 million player option for next season.

A six-time All-Star, Towns was a catalyst for the Knicks' playoff run last season, averaging 15.9 points, 10.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists as New York ended a 53-year title drought with a five-game Finals victory over the San Antonio Spurs.

Towns, who turns 31 in November, was asked if he wanted to table contract talks when the season begins so that it wouldn't be a distraction.

"In this situation, there's no comfortability to be had," he said.

Towns' potential extension is at the intersection of the Knicks keeping their championship core together and staying underneath the punitive second apron -- it already cost the team backup center Mitchell Robinson, who signed with the Boston Celtics this summer.

"On my grandkid, I couldn't, you ask me to give three facts or two facts about the second apron, I can't do it," Towns said. "I have no interest in that. It is what it is. [Knicks team president] Leon (Rose) trusts me with stuff on the court and I trust him with that stuff."

But he knows these issues can fester through the season. Towns said he won't ignore them.

"The first thing is we try to talk about everything. We don't leave any elephants in the room," Towns said. "They'll figure it out and our group has done a fantastic job of understanding that we can only control what we can control."

Towns isn't the only starter with a looming contract, as Josh Hart is eligible for an extension. Hart will make $20.9 million this season and there's a team option for $22.3 million in 2027-28.

Hart mentioned the second apron and collective bargaining agreement that has played a part in the NBA having eight champions in eight years, with the Knicks hoping to buck that trend. The challenge could be made tougher in a deeper, top-heavy Eastern Conference and the Knicks' own contractual issues.

"When there's uncertainty, there's gonna be a lot of questions," Hart said. "Rumors and at a human level it can wear people down and it can affect how you handle business on a daily basis. You want to get it done so you don't have to deal with that. At the end of the day it's a business. For me, as long as I'm wearing this jersey I'm gonna play as hard as I can. Hopefully we can figure that out."

Sept. 28

Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles

The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles in Brandon Ingram's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season.

Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year"

Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's Media Day.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me."

Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday at the Golden State Warriors' Media Day, including positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element," but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer, addressed the media on Monday, including questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks

articles.headline: NFL trade deadline grades: J.J. McCarthy to the Giants
articles.description: Can J.J. McCarthy improve the Giants' QB situation? Did the Vikings get enough back? We're grading NFL trades ahead of November's deadline.
articles.body:
Let's grade deals ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline, which will pass on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET.

When grading trades, I evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

Here's my take and evaluation of the J.J. McCarthy deal that kicked off trading season. Check back right through the deadline for grades on the biggest moves.

Vikings send QB McCarthy to Giants

Giants get: QB J.J. McCarthy

Vikings get: 2027 fifth-round pick

Giants grade: C

Vikings grade: B+

A mere 22 days after the Giants signed Jameis Winston to a two-year, $13 million extension, New York decided it needed to trade a fifth-round pick for an alternative at quarterback. Of course, a lot has happened in three weeks.

Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury in Week 2 that is expected to keep him out for at least the regular season. And Winston has delivered two poor performances in Dart's stead, with a 19.0 QBR in relief in Week 2 against the Rams and a 27.9 in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans. So in comes McCarthy, the No. 10 pick in the 2024 draft.

McCarthy's pro career has gone poorly so far, which is putting it mildly. He suffered a season-ending knee injury in August 2024, which helped Sam Darnold become Minnesota's starting quarterback. McCarthy was named the starter last season after Darnold departed in free agency but started only 10 games after a series of injuries cost him time. And when he was on the field, the results were not good.

McCarthy posted a 36.1 QBR in 2025 (which ranked 38th out of 45 quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts) and recorded a minus-5% pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats (43rd out of 45). He threw interceptions at a 4.2% clip (44th), took sacks on 9.4% of dropbacks (40th) and had a 1.8% fumble rate (41st). More alarming is that he did all that while playing for Kevin O'Connell, who has seemingly elevated most of the non-McCarthy quarterbacks he has called plays for.

During training camp, not only did McCarthy lose the Vikings' starting quarterback competition to Kyler Murray, but he then lost the backup competition to Carson Wentz, too. That is a telling red flag.

So why would the Giants trade for him? McCarthy presumably still has some upside based on his draft pedigree, and the Giants are hoping they can profit from him realizing it. But it's hard not to notice the fact that this is John Harbaugh trading for the quarterback his brother, Jim Harbaugh, coached in college at Michigan.

articles.description: How do QB moves in New York and Tampa Bay affect the Giants' and Bucaneers' receivers?
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 28: QB-depleted Giants trade for J.J. McCarthy, Bucs lose Baker Mayfield

By Eric Karabell

Quarterback J.J. McCarthy, the No. 10 pick in the 2024 NFL draft, is now a member of the New York Giants after they sent a fifth-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings for his services. In some ways, this is stunning. The Vikings gave up on McCarthy after one terrible season in which he completed only 57.6% of his throws and accrued more interceptions than touchdown passes. He is 23, but the Vikings might or might not be set with their future quarterback depending on how newcomer Kyler Murray performs. Early returns -- for Murray's performance and durability -- are quite mixed.

The Giants are taking a chance on an intriguing prospect even though McCarthy did not play well during his first active season. Then again, the Giants already have an intriguing quarterback prospect in Jaxson Dart, the No. 25 pick in the 2025 draft. Dart remains their future quarterback, but concussions marred his rookie campaign, and this season ended in Week 2 with major tears in his left knee. Nobody knows whether Dart can stay healthy for a full season, which is why this trade makes sense for the Giants.

For fantasy purposes, those who roster Dart in a keeper/dynasty league should already have been quite worried about his future in terms of staying on the field. This trade doesn't necessarily alter that. McCarthy missed his entire rookie season with a knee injury, too. The Giants add another body who, when healthy, needs to prove himself on the field. Dart has done that part already.

As for this season's Giants, veteran backup Jameis Winston seems likely to remain the starting quarterback for as long as he is healthy and competent. He was competent enough Sunday, leading the team to a 12-7 win over the Titans, even though he did little to aid fantasy managers statistically. Winston threw for only 118 yards, albeit in difficult weather conditions, but he avoided turnovers. The Winston who passed for 5,109 yards, 33 touchdowns and 30 interceptions for the 2019 Buccaneers is long gone.

Expect Winston to remain the starter, and assuming the Giants prefer Winston to act cautiously as a passer, merely directing the offense and attempting safe throws, it already impedes the upside for WRs Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields, and TE Isaiah Likely. articles.headline: Kawhi Leonard focused on being a Raptor after Clippers exit
articles.description: Kawhi Leonard said he wants to put the focus on basketball and being a Raptor after being traded back to Toronto following a scandal-marred conclusion to his Clippers tenure.
articles.body:
The last time Kawhi Leonard was at Toronto Raptors media day, he was seen as a mercenary player whose laugh became a meme. Now, eight years later, he is excited to be back and looking to put behind him a scandal and investigation that put one final cloud over his seven-season LA Clippers tenure.

"I'm excited to be here. I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation, but you know, talking with the NBA and the [NBPA], I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," Leonard said Monday.

Leonard's contract that he signed as a free agent after his one previous season in Toronto became the subject of a nearly yearlong investigation that concluded this offseason. The Clippers were found to have participated in salary cap circumvention -- agreeing to get Leonard extra money outside of his NBA contract through team-brokered, no-work endorsement deals.

Clippers owner Steve Ballmer has been suspended by the NBA for one year, with two other executives also handed suspensions. Leonard, a two-time NBA Finals MVP, wasn't suspended but must pay the league $700,000.

The investigation held up an agreed-upon trade that ultimately was approved by the league. In the end, Toronto sent last year's leading scorer Brandon Ingram, former lottery pick Gradey Dick and multiple picks back to Los Angeles for Leonard. The Raptors and 35-year-old Leonard subsequently agreed to a two-year, $115 million contract extension.

"I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet with my teammates, do any of that minicamp stuff with them," Leonard said Monday. "So, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors today."

Leonard's 2018-19 season in Toronto was one of his best. Over 60 regular-season games, he averaged 26.6 points and a career-best 7.3 rebounds, and he won NBA Finals MVP for the second time while leading the Raptors to their only championship.

Last season, Leonard played in 65 games and averaged a career-high 27.9 rebounds to go with 6.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists. He earned his seventh All-Star selection and was voted second-team All-NBA.

Leonard's return trip to the Clippers comes Nov. 2, but that is the second game of a back-to-back.
